+def _update_stats(stats, s, pat, pair, idx):
+    """
+    Update pair counts (stats of s) in place so they become the stats of
+    s.replace(pat, chr(idx)), where s holds one character chr(id) per token,
+    pat = chr(pair[0]) + chr(pair[1]) and idx does not occur in s. str.find
+    visits the occurrences left to right without overlaps, exactly like
+    merge(). Only pairs touching a merged occurrence change; zero counts are
+    removed.
+    """
+    p0, p1 = pair
+    get = stats.get
+    n = len(s)
+    find = s.find
+    removed = [pair]
+    rapp = removed.append
+    k = 0
+    end = -1 # end of the previous occurrence
+    j = find(pat)
+    while j >= 0:
+        k += 1
+        if j and j != end:
+            # left neighbour is untouched (an adjacent previous occurrence
+            # already accounted for the pair between them)
+            a = ord(s[j-1])
+            p = (a, p0)
+            stats[p] -= 1
+            rapp(p)
+            p = (a, idx)
+            stats[p] = get(p, 0) + 1
+        end = j + 2
+        if end < n:
+            b = ord(s[end])
+            p = (p1, b)
+            stats[p] -= 1
+            rapp(p)
+            j = find(pat, end)
+            # the right neighbour is merged too if the next occurrence follows
+            p = (idx, idx if j == end else b)
+            stats[p] = get(p, 0) + 1
+        else:
+            j = -1
+    stats[pair] -= k

actions.reason: BasicTokenizer.train now keeps the token sequence as a str with one character per token, chr(id). A merge becomes a single str.replace, which replaces left to right without overlaps, the same as merge(). The stats update and the tie-break use str.find, so they visit only real pair occurrences instead of every occurrence of p0 in Python. Stats are updated in the same order with the same values, and ties still go to the earliest occurrence. Evaluate: outputs identical, train_ir ratio 0.7232, encode_ir unchanged (1.0010).
